findings.evidence: `Basic.lean:111-112` defines `realOperator (t : ℝ) := S t.toNNReal`; Mathlib has `continuous_real_toNNReal` at `Mathlib/Topology/Instances/NNReal/Lemmas.lean:58`, and the existing `Basic.lean:408-410` gives the positive half-line continuity needed away from zero.
findings.fix: Prove `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_continuous (S) (x) : Continuous (fun t : ℝ => S.realOperator t x)` first, then derive this `ContinuousOn` wrapper if it is still wanted.
findings.issue: `realOperator_continuousOn_nonnegative` only states continuity on `Set.Ici 0`, but `S.realOperator` is defined on all `ℝ` by composing with `Real.toNNReal`.

findings.evidence: `Basic.lean:105-107` gives the native orbit continuity at `0`, composing with `continuous_real_toNNReal` handles `t = 0`; for `t < 0`, `Real.toNNReal` is locally constant equal to `0`, while `Basic.lean:408-410` already handles `t > 0`.
findings.fix: Replace it with or derive it from `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_continuousAt (S) (x) (t : ℝ) : ContinuousAt (fun u : ℝ => S.realOperator u x) t` with no positivity hypothesis.
findings.issue: `realOperator_continuousAt_of_pos` requires `0 < t`, but the same real-time shim is continuous at `t = 0` and at negative `t` as well.

summary: The new orbit-continuity wrappers are under-generalized for the public `realOperator` shim. Since the shim is defined on all real times via `Real.toNNReal`, the natural public theorem is all-real continuity, with the half-line and positive-time forms derived as special cases.
